description: Eighteen invented lesson objectives standing in for the rough notes a teacher writes before a lesson, so drafting and feedback support can be looked at without using anyone's real planning or any pupil's work.

records.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
records.draftObjective: By the end of the lesson most of them should be able to find a fraction of a whole number without drawing it out first.

records.subject: Language and Literacy
records.draftObjective: Pupils write a short recount of the trip in the right order, using at least three time words from the wall.

records.subject: The World Around Us
records.draftObjective: I want them to be able to say why we would not make a window out of wood, in their own words rather than mine.

records.subject: The World Around Us
records.draftObjective: Might need two lessons for this. Pupils use a simple key to mark four features of the local area on a sketch map.

records.subject: The Arts
records.draftObjective: Pupils mix three shades of the same colour and tell me what they changed each time.

records.subject: Mathematics
records.draftObjective: Pupils solve an equation with the unknown on both sides and check the answer by putting it back in.

records.subject: English
records.draftObjective: By the end of the double period they should be able to tell the difference between an opinion stated firmly and an opinion backed up with something.

records.subject: Science
records.draftObjective: Pupils explain what happens to the particles when ice melts, without saying that the particles themselves melt.

records.subject: Geography
records.draftObjective: Pupils should be able to explain, in their own words, why the river slows down where the valley widens out.

records.subject: History
records.draftObjective: Pupils read two accounts of the same event and say which one they trust more, and why.

records.subject: Technology and Design
records.draftObjective: Pupils name who their product is for and two things that person actually needs from it.

records.subject: Learning for Life and Work
records.draftObjective: Pupils work out what is left once the fixed costs come off a weekly budget, then say what they would cut first and defend it.

records.subject: Modern Languages
records.draftObjective: Pupils describe their own morning routine out loud for about a minute, with the prompts still on the board.

records.subject: Music
records.draftObjective: Pupils keep a steady pulse in a group while one of them changes the rhythm over the top of it.

records.subject: Mathematics
records.draftObjective: Pupils work out a percentage increase and, more importantly, notice when the question is really asking for the original amount.

records.subject: English Language
records.draftObjective: Pupils write one paragraph comparing how both writers open their article, with a short quotation from each.

records.subject: Chemistry
records.draftObjective: Pupils plan a fair test for the effect of temperature on rate and say out loud which variables they are holding still.

records.subject: Religious Studies
records.draftObjective: Pupils set out two views on the question fairly before giving their own, and say what would change their mind.
